title: ComplyBoard: signoff lattice for shadow, canary and A/B rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce 'ComplyBoard' — a declarative signoff lattice and evidence-bundle model to govern model promotions for shadow traffic, canary slices, and A/B tests. The goal is to standardize required signoffs, RBAC gates, and audit artifacts so every production promotion has machine-verifiable authorization, a tamper-evident audit bundle, and well-defined auto-rollback knobs tied to the approval state. This ticket captures the product spec, acceptance criteria, and implementation handoff requirements for PM/Eng/Design collaboration.
acceptance_criteria: A ComplyBoard model is definable per model release that enumerates required roles (e.g., engineer, SRE, security, product) and the minimum evidence per role.
Deploy-time gate enforcement is implemented: a canary/capacity rollout will not advance stages without required signoffs recorded in the audit bundle.
Audit bundles include: signatory id, timestamp, justification note, linked e2e/runbook checklist, PR link, and snapshot of rollout config; bundles are stored immutable with tamper-evidence metadata.
RBAC policies are plumbed to the Console so signoff buttons only appear for authorized principals; logs show which principal approved which stage.
Auto-rollback triggers (latency regression, error-rate spike, metric drift) can run regardless of signoff state but will notify signatories and attach rollback evidence to the same audit bundle.
A/B experiments and shadow traffic promotions can require a reduced signoff path (product + SRE) based on a risk-level policy; those policies are configurable per workspace.
Operational runbook and UI flows are reviewed and accepted by Design, Eng, Security, and Compliance teams.
A migration plan exists to convert existing rollouts (canaries and A/B) to reference ComplyBoard targets with minimal disruption.
proposed_workflow: 1) Author creates a ComplyBoard spec for a model promotion with named stages (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> full). 2) For each stage the spec lists required roles and evidence types (e.g., 'SRE: canary perf dashboard snapshot', 'Security: static config review link', 'PM: behavioral eval summary'). 3) System creates an immutable evidence bundle per stage. 4) Signatories approve through Console; approvals recorded with principal, timestamp, and optional note. 5) Rollout automation respects approvals: stages cannot auto-advance if flagged as 'manual-approval-required'. 6) If auto-rollback triggers fire at any stage, rollback is executed, the bundle is updated with rollback evidence, and all signatories are notified for postmortem steps.
rbac_matrix: Platform Admin: full override permission (bypass allowed, audited).
Release Engineer: can create ComplyBoard specs, start/pause rollouts, and provide SRE signoff.
SRE: required to sign for canary and ramp stages for production model types.
Product Manager: required for behavioral / quality signoff on A/B and feature rollouts.
Security/Compliance: required signoff for private/VPC deployments and any model with 'sensitive-data' label.
Observer: read-only; can attach evidence but cannot sign.
audit_log_requirements: Immutable evidence bundle per stage stored in the workspace's audit store (append-only).
Bundle items: signatory principal, role, timestamp (ISO8601), freeform justification, links to artifact (GitHub PR, Confluence doc, dashboard snapshot), rollout config hash.
Audit entries must be queryable by model id, rollout id, principal, and time range in Console.
Retention policy: default 1 year; enterprise customers can choose longer retention.
Tamper-evidence: bundles include chain-of-hash metadata; any change triggers an integrity alert sent to Security.
auto_rollback_policy: Pre-configured triggers: p50 latency > baseline + 2x IQR, error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline, embedding-regression score drop >= 5pts versus baseline eval set.
Thresholds adjustable per rollout stage and model risk level.
Rollback action: immediate stage revert to last stable model variant; optional blackhole of traffic if revert fails.
Rollback notifications: immediate webhook to PagerDuty, e-mail+Console notification to signatories and workspace admins.
Post-rollback: system opens a postmortem ticket template (pre-populated with audit bundle and metric diffs) and requires at least one signatory to acknowledge within 72 hours.
